item.content:encoded:
Team Fiji weightlifter Taniela Rainibogi has just won Fiji's first gold medal at the 2026 Glasgow Commonwealth Games in the 110kg division as well as breaking three Games records.

Rainibogi had a record total of 378kg, lifting 170kg in the snatch and 208kg in the clean and jerk â€“ both Commonwealth Games records.

His winning total pushed England's Cyrille Tchatchet II into silver with 374kg while Canada's Xavier Lusignan claimed bronze with 356kg.

Rainibogi's victory continues a memorable week for Pacific weightlifting after SÄmoa's Seine Stowers claimed gold and Games records in the women's 77kg division and SÄmoa's John Tafi opened his country's medal tally with silver.

Fiji's success does not end on the weightlifting platform with young boxer Jasmine Daunakamakama also keeping the country's medal charge alive.

Daunakamakama defeated Singapore's Keshani Hansika in the women's 57kg quarter-final to secure at least a bronze medal, becoming Fiji's first female boxer guaranteed a podium finish.

The 21-year-old, who is also Fiji's first woman to compete internationally in boxing, said her strength comes from mana.

Daunakamakama will face Northern Ireland's Michaela Walsh in theÂ Women's 57kg semi-finals at 1.30am tomorrow.

In Lawn Bowls, Women's Singles Sectional: Elizabeth Moceiwai lost her first game to Tonga's Milika Nathan 1.5-0.5.

Moceiwai also went down Norfolk Island's Shae Wilson 2-0.

In the Men's Pairs Sectional: Fiji lost to Australia 2-0.

Their next match is at 7.40am against Pakistan.

Australia currently leads the medal tally with 49 gold, 22 silver, and 35 bronze, Canda is second with 14 gold, 11 silver, and 16 bronze, while England is third with 13 gold, 28 silver and 18 bronze.

item.title: Retired Police Officer recounts emotional wait as missing daughter is found safe
item.description: Timoci Lutunauga, the father of Maca Lutunauga, a Health Inspector with the Ministry of Health who was among the group reported missing at sea, struggled to hold back his emotions as he recounted the family's ordeal. While speaking to fijivillage News, the retired police officer says he had never cried in his life, but was devastated when he received a call informing him that his eldest daughter w
item.content:encoded:
Timoci Lutunauga, the father of Maca Lutunauga, a Health Inspector with the Ministry of Health who was among the group reported missing at sea, struggled to hold back his emotions as he recounted the family's ordeal.

While speaking to fijivillage News, the retired police officer says he had never cried in his life, but was devastated when he received a call informing him that his eldest daughter was drifting at sea.

He says he was unable to sleep or eat for the past 48 hours.

Lutunauga shared that he told his family he could not bring himself to eat while knowing his daughter was out at sea without food.

Drawing on his experience as a former police officer who had travelled extensively, including throughout the Lau Group, he says he understood just how harsh and cold conditions at sea could be.

Throughout the ordeal, the father of two kept his family united through daily devotions, praying constantly for the safety of those missing.

When news finally came that the group had been found, he said he could no longer contain his emotions and gave thanks to God for His mercy and love.

Lutunauga also expressed his heartfelt gratitude to the people of Lau, who used their own boats and resources to assist in the search, as well as the Fiji Navy and all other agencies including the Lomaiviti Princess 12 crew and individuals involved in the rescue efforts.

Timoci Lutunauga lives with his wife and their two daughters.

item.title: Ra women's group turns farming training into thriving nursery business
item.description: Women from Navolau No. 1 Village in Ra are turning agricultural training into a sustainable business after becoming an approved supplier of vegetable and fruit seedlings to the Ministry of Agriculture, Waterways and Sugar Industry, following training in Sustainable Land Management and Farm Management. The Marama ni Navutalakise Cluster, which is part of the Yavusa Burenitu, recently completed the
item.content:encoded:
Women from Navolau No. 1 Village in Ra are turning agricultural training into a sustainable business after becoming an approved supplier of vegetable and fruit seedlings to the Ministry of Agriculture, Waterways and Sugar Industry, following training in Sustainable Land Management and Farm Management.

The Marama ni Navutalakise Cluster, which is part of the Yavusa Burenitu, recently completed the training facilitated by the Ministry, gaining practical skills in nursery management, seedling production and sustainable farming practices.

The training has already produced results, with the women's group now recognised as an approved vendor to supply vegetable and fruit seedlings to the Ministry in Ra Province.

The achievement provides the cluster with a sustainable source of income while supporting the Ministry's efforts to improve farmers' access to quality planting materials across the province.

To help meet the growing demand for seedlings and maintain the required quality standards, the cluster worked closely with Ministry officials to establish a nursery.

The new nursery will allow the group to increase seedling production, improve efficiency and ensure a reliable supply of healthy, high-quality vegetable and fruit seedlings.

It is also expected to strengthen the long-term sustainability of the business while creating more economic opportunities for the women involved.

Cluster President Alena Beraua says the Sustainable Land Management and Farm Management training has given members the knowledge and confidence to improve their farming activities and pursue new income-generating opportunities.

Beraua says becoming a recognised supplier to the Ministry is a proud achievement that reflects the dedication and hard work of the group's members.

She says the training has equipped them with the skills to produce quality seedlings and manage their nursery more effectively, adding that they are committed to maintaining the standards expected by the Ministry.

Beraua says the establishment of the nursery has given the women the confidence to expand their operations and meet the increasing demand for quality planting materials.

She says the group's vision is to grow the nursery into a reliable supplier of quality planting materials while creating more economic opportunities for women in the cluster.

Beraua adds they hope their success will inspire other women's groups to embrace agriculture as a pathway to sustainable livelihoods, while benefiting farming communities throughout Ra Province.

The Ministry of Agriculture, Waterways and Sugar Industry says it will continue supporting community-based groups through training and capacity-building programmes that empower women, promote climate-smart agriculture and create sustainable livelihood opportunities.

item.title: Mother shares son's cancer journey to encourage early diagnosis
item.description: 7-year-old Jeremiah Tuiraviravi was one of seven childhood cancer survivors present at the launch of Childhood Cancer Awareness Month 2026, organised by WOWS Kids Fiji, with his journey serving as a powerful reminder of the importance of early detection. Tuiraviravi was just five years old when he was diagnosed with orbital sarcoma, a cancer affecting the eye, in 2024.
item.content:encoded:
7-year-old Jeremiah Tuiraviravi was one of seven childhood cancer survivors present at the launch of Childhood Cancer Awareness Month 2026, organised by WOWS Kids Fiji, with his journey serving as a powerful reminder of the importance of early detection.

Tuiraviravi was just five years old when he was diagnosed with orbital sarcoma, a cancer affecting the eye, in 2024.

Speaking to fijivillage News, his mother Victoria Taria says that after undergoing a long period of treatment in hospital, her son is now on his five-year post-chemotherapy follow-up journey and is a healthy boy awaiting his regular reviews.

Taria says if his cancer does not return after the five-year post-chemotherapy period, he will be considered a survivor.

She says although he is now a healthy boy, returning to school has been one of his biggest challenges.

Taria says she is grateful for the support provided by WOWS Kids Fiji, including providing private tutoring to help her son get back to normal with his education.

She says WOWS Kids Fiji has supported their family throughout Tuiraviravi's medical journey by providing medication that was not available through the hospital, transport to and from medical appointments, counselling, and education support for children returning to school after treatment.

Taria is urging parents and guardians to take their children to hospital when they are sick, saying early detection can save a child's life.

Meanwhile, s peaking at the launch, Assistant Minister for Health and Medical Services Penioni Ravunawa highlighted that every child deserves the opportunity to grow, dream and live a healthy life.

item.title: Sanday reveals Flying Fijians players sought $1,000 daily allowance, but Fiji Rugby could not afford it - Sanday
item.description: Fiji Rugby Chair John Sanday says the FIJI Water Flying Fijians players had asked for an increase in allowance from $500 a day to $1,000 per day during their Nations Championship Tour in Europe. In an interview with fijivillage Play With Alipate Narawa, Sanday stated that this is a normal employer and employee situation that the players were requesting and some of that the FRU was able to deliver
item.content:encoded:
Fiji Rugby Chair John Sanday says the FIJI Water Flying Fijians players had asked for an increase in allowance from $500 a day to $1,000 per day during their Nations Championship Tour in Europe.

In an interview with fijivillage Play With Alipate Narawa, Sanday stated that this is a normal employer and employee situation that the players were requesting and some of that the FRU was able to deliver like Business Class seats for the players.

He says on the payment side, they were not able to deliver on the $1,000 a day because they are not in a financial position, and they are talking about a 40 man squad.

The FRU Chair says some of them have been working on the Board for 2 years, and they have given their 100 percent but have not been paid a cent.

He says it is a conversation, adding that if they had won, then they would have been paid.

When queried on this not being the first time that players have held the FRU hostage based on pay, Sanday says it is the first time for him, although he knows it has happened several times before.

Sanday says it is not something he likes to entertain.

He says if the team performs, then they will be happy to pay them.

item.title: 10-month-old baby youngest of 64 children supported by WOWS Kids Fiji
item.description: A 10-month-old baby is the youngest of the 64 children currently receiving support from WOWS Kids Fiji, highlighting the need for parents to recognise the early signs of childhood cancer. Speaking at the launch of Childhood Cancer Awareness Month 2026, WOWS Kids Fiji board member Anabel Ali says the organisation is currently caring for 64 children battling cancer across Fiji, including 43 boys and
item.content:encoded:
A 10-month-old baby is the youngest of the 64 children currently receiving support from WOWS Kids Fiji, highlighting the need for parents to recognise the early signs of childhood cancer.

Speaking at the launch of Childhood Cancer Awareness Month 2026, WOWS Kids Fiji board member Anabel Ali says the organisation is currently caring for 64 children battling cancer across Fiji, including 43 boys and 21 girls.

Ali says WOWS Kids Fiji has lost five children since January this year and sees around 30 new childhood cancer cases annually.

She says the number of children affected by childhood cancer could be higher, as some cases may be managed directly through hospitals or private institutions.

She says the focus of Childhood Cancer Awareness Month is to educate parents, caregivers, teachers, and communities about the early warning signs of childhood cancer and the importance of seeking medical attention early.

INSERT: Ali on early detection 30th July

Ali says Fiji launches Childhood Cancer Awareness Month in August, a month ahead of the global campaign in September, to give more people an opportunity to learn about the warning signs of childhood cancer and the importance of early diagnosis and treatment.

She says WOWS Kids Fiji is not a medical organisation but works alongside health professionals to ensure children and their families receive the support they need throughout treatment.

She says the organisation assists families with transport, medical supplies when hospitals are unable to provide them, nutritional support, counselling, educational assistance, and private tutoring for children who are away from school during treatment.

Ali says the organisation also supports caregivers, an aspect that is often overlooked, through food assistance, counselling, laundry services, and opportunities for self-care.

She stresses that early detection can make a difference, noting that some children have recovered after receiving timely treatment.

She is urging parents and communities to pay attention to changes in children and seek medical advice as soon as concerns arise.
